dct_description_sm: Permafrost occurs in large areas of northern Scandinavia, it is particularly prevalent at high altitudes. Permafrost can be said to be ground that is frozen for at least two consecutive years, it is ground with permafrost. In cold areas, such as in Siberia and northern Canada may permafrost may extend several hundred meters into the ground. The upper layer soil thaws in summer, the layer is called the active layer. The depth of the active layer varies depending on soil characteristics, such as how much water it contains. Peat which can contain a lot of water has an active storage of about 1 m while the moraine is a mineral soil can not hold as much water and therefore have a thinner active layer of about 0.5 m Landscape with permafrost have often characteristic terrain. The result of permafrost in lowland terrain, landforms palsas , Pingos , circular or polygonal frost cracks and ice wedges in the underlying land. Measurements of soil temperatures and permafrost are informative about today's climate, but are also very useful variables to predict future climate scenarios as well as understanding the past.
dct_title_s: The eye of Abisko (Abiskogat) - permafrost and soil temperature
